obligations.statement: The product must accept a force from the user's foot to move from resting to an actuated position.
derivation_premises: The machine receives a signal only if a force is applied to the pedal.

obligations.statement: The product must return to its resting position on its own when the user's foot is removed.
derivation_premises: The pedal will not return to rest unless an internal mechanism provides a restoring force.

obligations.statement: The product must resist transverse forces applied sideways without moving from its resting position.
derivation_premises: The pedal would move sideways if the transverse force exceeds the static friction or geometric restraint.

obligations.statement: The product must communicate a signal to the machine.
derivation_premises: The pedal must be coupled to the machine somehow to transmit a signal.

obligations.statement: The product must be able to be mounted to a workbench.
derivation_premises: The pedal must be attached to the workbench to be useful.

candidates.summary: A hinged pedal with a spring return and an electrical signal.

evidence_route_verdict.note: A revolute joint with a torsion spring is a simple mechanism to model.

candidates.summary: A sliding pedal with a spring return and an electrical signal.

evidence_route_verdict.note: A prismatic joint with a return spring can be modeled with ideal joints.

candidates.summary: A compliant flexure pedal with spring return and electrical signal.

evidence_route_verdict.note: Detailed compliance analysis is not available at this stage.

assumptions.statement: The foot pedal is intended to be operated by a human foot.
assumptions.why: The request says 'I take my foot off'.
assumptions.would_be_invalidated_by: If the pedal is operated by other means

assumptions.statement: The machine is external to the foot pedal.
assumptions.why: The request says 'send a signal to the machine'.

assumptions.statement: The pedal is mounted to the workbench.
